claims.claim: Gregory Thaumaturgus was bishop of Neocaesarea in Pontus.
Gregory Thaumaturgus was born around 213 and died around 270.
Gregory Thaumaturgus was also known as Gregory of Neocaesarea and was called 'the wonder-worker' (Thaumaturgus).
The work 'On the Subject of the Soul' is addressed to Tatian.
Tatian requested the discourse on the soul and asked that it be written without using the testimonies of Scripture.

Tatian wanted the work not for his own assurance, since he was already taught by Holy Scriptures and traditions, but for confuting men who do not admit credit to the Scriptures and who use clever speech to gain over the unversed.
The work was written in response to philosophers and heretics with whom Christians daily came into conflict.
The work survives under the title 'On the Subject of the Soul' (Disputatio de anima ad Tatianum) and is included in the Ante-Nicene Fathers collection.
Gregory's theological writings have reached us in a very incomplete state.
Gregory studied with Origen at Caesarea in Palestine for about five years, probably 233-238.
Gregory was originally named Theodore and was born to a pagan family.
